title: Preemptive reservoir policy for batched streams with KV dilution control
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Continuous batching improves per-token throughput but suffers when long-lived KV residents (large context or many simultaneous tenants) cause memory pressure and unpredictable tail latency. Current preemption heuristics tend to be all-or-nothing: evict entire KV working sets or hard-kill slices, which gives poor fairness and causes SLO regressions for latency-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement a preemptive reservoir policy that probabilistically drains batch admission and KV residency for candidates to create short, controlled interruptions that reclaim memory while preserving proportional SLO guarantees. Add a KV dilution control layer to prioritize retention of hot prefixes and reduce cache churn. The combination should reduce P95/P99 tail latency regressions under high memory pressure and improve fairness across tenant classes without large throughput loss.
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir policy implemented in preemptor service and feature-flag gated
KV dilution control heuristics integrated into cache manager and exposed as tunables
Load tests show <=10% throughput regression and >=20% improvement in P99 for latency-sensitive tenants on mixed workloads compared to baseline preemptor
No customer-facing errors introduced; fallback path to previous preemptor via feature flag
End-to-end integration tests covering eviction, preemption, and resident promotion pass in CI
tasks: Design algorithm and data structures for reservoir scoring (Aisha)
Proto implementation of reservoir admission gate in preemptor service (Marco)
Add KV dilution metrics and signals to cache manager (Jules)
Simulate mixed-tenant workloads offline and collect fairness/latency curves (Eng-Perf)
Implement feature flag and rollout toggles in control plane (SRE)
E2E test harness for memory-pressure scenarios (QA)
Create dashboard panels for reservoir health and KV dilution metrics (Observability)
Prepare internal doc and runbook for rollback (PM/Support)
design_notes: Reservoir policy is a time-windowed probabilistic admission controller: each incoming stream is assigned a reservoir token budget proportional to its SLO weight; when memory pressure crosses thresholds the admission probability decays gracefully instead of deterministic denial.
Tokens are replenished on completed slices and decayed for long-lived KV entries; small token refunds are applied for short-latency completions to encourage low-latency work.

KV dilution control tags cache entries with a small hotness vector (recent access count, tenant weight, prefix-affinity). Eviction score = base_age_factor * dilution_penalty, where dilution_penalty favors keeping high-affinity prefixes even if their raw recency is lower.
We will avoid global locks by sharding reservoir state per-GPU and using lock-free counters with periodic cross-shard reconciliation for fairness guarantees.

Preemption is soft: when a reservoir step requests reclaim, we first attempt 'micro-yield' (pause/resume) for streaming slices using lightweight checkpointing of decoder state; full eviction only as last resort. This reduces KV churn and improves tail behavior.

To balance fairness, each tenant is assigned a configurable weight; the reservoir algorithm enforces proportional decrease in admission probability during congestion rather than absolute deprioritization.
Edge case: very large single requests (long sequences) can monopolize tokens; we impose an upper bound per-slice token allocation and break long sequences into resumable micro-slices where possible.
We will surface three tunables: memory_pressure_thresholds, reservoir_decay_rate, and dilution_penalty_factor. Defaults chosen from simulation sweeps but adjustable per-tenant in Dedicated mode.
test_plan: Unit tests for reservoir token accounting and deterministic replay of probabilistic decisions
Integration tests: synthetic mix of latency-sensitive (chat) and throughput-heavy (batch embed) tenants under controlled memory pressure
Chaos tests: simulate GPU OOM, KV corruption, and preemptor restart during high load
Performance benchmarks: end-to-end throughput, P50/P95/P99 latency curves, KV hit rate and churn rate comparisons
Fairness validation: measure per-tenant slowdown and ensure proportionality within 10% of target weights
A/B release: Canary on 10% of traffic in a single region, compare against baseline for 72 hours before ramp
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge to main behind runtime-1.24 branch
Canary rollout: start with internal accounts and staging clusters (10%)
Collect telemetry for 48-72 hours: reservoir acceptance rate, KV retention distribution, tail latencies
If metrics pass, expand to 30% then 60% over two weeks with automated rollback on threshold breaches
Final 100% rollout coordinated with support and SRE, with 24/7 on-call for first 48 hours
Post-rollout retrospective and tuning pass to update tunables and defaults
metrics: reservoir_accept_rate_by_tenant: percentage of admitted slices per tenant
kv_retention_entropy: measure of KV spread vs focused hot prefixes
gpu_free_memory_headroom: realtime memory available vs thresholds
p95_latency_latency_sensitive: end-to-end P95 for SLO class
p99_latency_all: end-to-end P99 across all tenants
